what: On first open, three words (a lowercase tagline) at the center of a background-color curtain light up one by one, delayed .2s·.4s·.6s, with a 1.5s ease and then stay. At 3.4s the curtain lifts in .3s, and from 3.6s the page body slowly brightens over 2s (jQuery swing) — a slow hero, like photo studio lights switching on. fx:open fires when the curtain starts lifting, fx:done when the body is fully bright.
ease: cubic-bezier(0.25,0.1,0.25,1) (word CSS ease) · sine.inOut (curtain·body jQuery swing)

options.[data-fx-part=word]: Words to light up in turn (child) — if none, only the curtain stays and then lifts
options.word: Duration for a single word to light up (sec), default 1.5
options.hold: Time the curtain starts lifting (s), default 3.4 — shorten for screens opened often
options.reveal: CSS selector for the body that brightens behind the curtain (e.g. main) — kept transparent as soon as it attaches, then switched on at reveal-at. If absent, only the event fires
options.reveal-at: Time when the body starts to brighten (sec), default 3.6
options.reveal-dur: Duration of the body brightening (sec), default 2
options.lock: if true, locks document scroll until reveal-at (the original pins body in place)

use: your three words
note: In the original, the CSS animation runs the moment inview adds .on to a word (within 250ms after load) — the part starts right on load

from.where: index.html .dm-loading (first page only — ‹Three Words› loader, the main .dm-main brightens over 2s starting at 3.6s and the menu button over .3s at 4.2s)
